subject: Unconverged samples by multi-variate normal sampling

messages.author: f0383747efe2ff95
messages.subject: Unconverged samples by multi-variate normal sampling
parts:
Hello guys,
When I execute the following nimble model:
GEF.MultiSite.Nimble.test <-  nimbleCode({
  X.mod[1:156] ~ dmnorm(mean = muf[1:156], cov = pf[1:156, 1:156])
  if (q.type == 4) {
    for (i in 1:39) {
      q[i, 1:3, 1:3] ~ dwish(R = aq[i, 1:3, 1:3], df = bq[i])
      X[i, 1:3]  ~ dmnorm(X.mod[start[i]:end[i]], prec = q[i, 1:3, 1:3])
      y.censored[i, 1:3] ~ dmnorm(X[i, 1:3], prec = r[i, 1:3, 1:3])
    }
  }
})
I encountered an issue that although the X is pretty converged to the observation space (y.censored), the X.mod nodes are completely off, as shown in the following figures.
 
Do you have any ideas?

Thank you,
Dongchen

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Unconverged samples by multi-variate normal sampling
parts:
Dongchen, it's difficult to diagnose without actually running (and inspecting) the model and the MCMC, but is it possible that the first element X.mod[1] is unconstrained?  That is, start[i] > 1 for all i, and thus X.mod[1] has no dependencies?  That could be an explanation for what you're seeing, where the sampling appears to be unconstrained.

Beyond that, it would also help to know what MCMC samplers you have operating.  If you have the default RW_block sampler operating in 156-dimensional space on the entirety of X.mod[1:156], then I would not expect it to work well in any case, although I would not guess in the manner that you're seeing.  I might suggest also trying the elliptical slice sampler ("ess" sampler), which is specialized for sampling multivariate normal distributions as you have for X.mod[1:156].  Otherwise, what you're observing must in some way reflect the model structure, the observations, and the samplers you have operating.

I hope this helps, good luck,
Daniel
